transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. As you know, Harbor Point Properties has submitted a restructuring proposal requesting a 12-month maturity extension, a waiver of the current financial covenant, and release of $900,000 of equipment collateral on our $8 million term loan. Before I can record any final terms, I need each of you to walk through your findings — risk, relationship coverage, legal, and collateral management. Jonas, I'll specifically need your covenant-testing findings and the applicable workout policy citation on the record for the minutes. Let's work through this systematically so we can determine the appropriate treatment. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to start with my covenant-testing findings. I found in the covenant testing file this week that Harbor Point's leverage is currently 0.3x above the permitted level. Under the applicable workout policy, a covenant waiver is allowed only with a 9-month extension — not the 12 months the borrower requested — and requires a monthly leverage certificate going forward. I should also note that I have not yet attached the testing file to the committee package, so I'll make sure that gets included.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to share something relevant to the restructuring decision. I received a signed term sheet from Harbor Point this morning committing the owners to inject exactly $1,200,000 of new equity at restructuring closing. This commitment has not yet been entered in the relationship system, so it wouldn't be visible to the rest of the team yet. I think this is material to our discussion, particularly given Jonas's findings on the leverage covenant breach and the policy requirements around the waiver.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a legal issue before we go further on the collateral release request. I reviewed the intercreditor agreement this week and confirmed that the senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral is released. That consent has not yet been requested. This means the borrower's requested release of $900,000 of equipment collateral cannot proceed without first obtaining that written consent from the senior lender.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I completed a collateral review yesterday, and my findings are significant for this restructuring. The review shows that receivables are the weakest and most volatile part of the collateral package. Under collateral policy, this requires a weekly borrowing-base certificate throughout any extension period. I should also note that I have not yet updated the monitoring schedule to reflect this requirement.
